pluss::NoGradGuard¶

Back to Series API Reference

Public Types¶

pluss::NoGradGuard guard;
pluss::AutoGradMode mode(bool enabled);
pluss::PauseRecording pause;

Include <pluss/pluss.h>.

These are scope guards. Construct one at the beginning of a block; its effect lasts until control leaves that block, including when an exception unwinds the stack.

What NoGradGuard Does¶

pluss::NoGradGuard temporarily stops new Series operations from joining the reverse graph. It is intended for work whose derivatives will never be needed: evaluation, reporting, validation metrics, data-dependent masks, and constants computed from tracked values.

The distinction is about operations, not about changing the input:

  • A Series that already tracks slope continues to do so.

  • A result computed from it while the guard is active does not track slope.

  • Once the guard leaves scope, later operations on the original Series are recorded normally again.

That makes the guard different from detach(). detach() returns one graph-independent view. NoGradGuard establishes a temporary policy for every operation in a lexical scope.

Choosing A Guard¶

pluss::NoGradGuard¶

Use this for the ordinary case: recording should be off for an entire block. It is concise, nestable, and restores the previous state automatically.

pluss::AutoGradMode¶

Use pluss::AutoGradMode(false) when code needs to choose the mode from a runtime condition. Use pluss::AutoGradMode(true) for a smaller nested block that must record even though an enclosing NoGradGuard disabled recording. On destruction, it restores the mode that was active before construction.

pluss::PauseRecording¶

pluss::PauseRecording also prevents new graph links, but it represents a temporary suspension rather than a mode choice. It is useful in reusable library code that must avoid recording its own bookkeeping without deciding whether the caller is generally in training or evaluation mode. Pauses are nestable and recording resumes only after the outermost pause ends.

For application code, prefer NoGradGuard. Reach for PauseRecording when writing infrastructure that may itself run inside another recording policy.

Examples¶

Evaluation Without Building A Reverse Graph¶

The input remains a tracked leaf, but the value produced inside the guarded scope is independent of the reverse graph.

auto weights = pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0, 4.0});
weights.tracks_slope_(true);

pluss::Series prediction;
{
  pluss::NoGradGuard guard;
  prediction = weights.square();
}

std::cout << "weights track: " << weights.tracks_slope() << "\n";
std::cout << "prediction tracks: " << prediction.tracks_slope() << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, prediction) << "\n";

Output¶

weights track: 1
prediction tracks: 0
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[4.0000, 9.0000, 16.0000]

The numerical calculation still occurs. Only graph construction is disabled.

Recording Resumes After The Scope¶

The same leaf can produce an untracked result inside the block and a tracked result immediately afterward.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

pluss::Series report;
{
  pluss::NoGradGuard guard;
  report = x.mul(10.0);
}

auto objective = x.square().sum();
objective.reverse();

std::cout << "report tracks: " << report.tracks_slope() << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity()) << "\n";

Output¶

report tracks: 0
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2.0000, 4.0000, 6.0000]

The report did not join the graph. The later objective did, so its reverse pass still produces 2 * x.

Enabling A Deliberate Inner Calculation¶

AutoGradMode(true) can restore recording for a carefully chosen inner block.

auto x = pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

pluss::Series outside_graph;
pluss::Series inside_graph;
{
  pluss::NoGradGuard guard;
  outside_graph = x.add(1.0);

  {
    pluss::AutoGradMode enable(true);
    inside_graph = x.square();
  }
}

std::cout << "outer result tracks: " << outside_graph.tracks_slope() << "\n";
std::cout << "inner result tracks: " << inside_graph.tracks_slope() << "\n";

Output¶

outer result tracks: 0
inner result tracks: 1

Keep such overrides narrow. A broad re-enable inside evaluation code can retain an unexpectedly large graph.

Suspending Bookkeeping Work¶

The pause guard is appropriate when a helper computes a diagnostic from a tracked value but must not alter the caller’s surrounding mode.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-2.0, 1.0, 4.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

pluss::Series positive_mask;
{
  pluss::PauseRecording pause;
  positive_mask = x.gt(0.0);
}

auto loss = x.square().sum();
loss.reverse();

std::cout << "mask tracks: " << positive_mask.tracks_slope() << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, positive_mask) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity()) << "\n";

Output¶

mask tracks: 0
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[false, true, true]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-4.0000, 2.0000, 8.0000]

The diagnostic mask remains usable as data. It simply has no reverse history.

Scope And Thread Rules¶

The guards are thread-local: disabling recording in one thread does not change another thread’s work. They are also nestable. Destruction restores the prior state rather than blindly enabling recording, so a helper can safely create a guard when its caller has already disabled recording.

Store these guards as local variables, not as long-lived global state. Their lexical lifetime is what makes restoration predictable and exception-safe.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • A guard does not erase an existing graph. Values built before the scope keep their reverse history.

  • tracks_slope_(true) inside a guarded block marks a leaf for later work, but operations performed before the guard ends are still not recorded.

  • An untracked result cannot later recover the operations that produced it. Recompute outside the guard if derivatives become necessary.

  • In-place mutation still mutates data. Disabling recording is not a rollback, copy, or immutability mechanism.

  • Keep AutoGradMode(true) blocks small so evaluation code does not retain a graph accidentally.

Summary¶

Use pluss::NoGradGuard to perform real Series computations without building new reverse links. Use pluss::AutoGradMode when the mode is selected explicitly, and pluss::PauseRecording for nestable infrastructure-level suspension. All three restore prior state automatically at scope exit.

See Also¶

  • Series::reverse: propagate sensitivities through recorded operations.

  • Series::tracks_slope: inspect whether a value is marked for reverse tracking.
